title: Create-a-class journey paints its primary controls from two color systems (token action vs inline account accent)
reference: Apple HIG Color re-read 2026-11-09 in browser: 'Avoid using the same color to mean different things. Use color consistently throughout your interface, especially when you use it to help communicate information like status or interactivity.' Supporting basis also studied live: Apple HIG Typography (legibility law — font size/weight impact how easy text is to read) and Apple HIG Layout (consistent layout law); the product's own WCAG 4.5:1 informative-text contrast law (FAP-30).
law: The create-a-class journey speaks one token color language: its interactive controls (empty-state CTA, modal submit, modal Cancel, modal field focus) paint from the workspace token system (--v-action #0071e3 light / #aac7ff dark, --v-on-action, single definition point). The account accent preference keeps personalizing supported learning views; it no longer redefines primary interactivity on the journey's controls. Copy, flow, field geometry, the class-color choices fieldset and the FAP-78 per-state singleton law untouched.
persona_note: Every probe run registered a REAL fresh teacher through the live register → onboarding journey (shared helper frontend/scripts/registerFixturePersona.mjs; helper landed in this ticket as instrument enablement). The green-accent stage sets the account accent through the product's own Settings → Account appearance path (input[name=accent] saved green in both runs, recorded as C0_saved). The modal submit was measured in BOTH its disabled state (dialog just opened) and its enabled state (name typed — the real ready-to-create state); the BEFORE side's inline style overrode the system disabled paint, so the same-state comparison is disabled-vs-disabled and enabled-vs-enabled.
